characterization_methods.key_findings: CR 50%: flattened/banded elongated grains with dense slip bands (Figure 2c); slip bands labelled 'Elongated grain' and 'Slip band'
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional samples ground and polished along RD, etched with hydrochloric acid (100 mL) + alcohol (100 mL) + copper chloride (5 g) etchant
characterization_methods.purpose: observe microstructural evolution with CR deformation

characterization_methods.key_findings: CR 50% fracture surface: uniformly distributed dimples of reduced size and depth relative to undeformed and CR 30% conditions
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: after tensile failure; 10 µm scale bar in fractographs

characterization_methods.key_findings: CR 50%: arrowed dark dislocation wall next to fine parallel lamellae labelled 'Deformation twin' (Figure 3c); dislocation entanglement and walls emerge; significant amount of deformation twins
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: samples mechanically ground to 60 μm slices, punched into Ф3 mm disks, ion-milled with Gatan 691
characterization_methods.purpose: observe dislocation structure and deformation twins

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D8 ADVANCE X-ray diffractometer with Cu-Kα radiation (λ = 0.15406 nm)
characterization_methods.key_findings: single-phase austenite maintained, no deformation-induced martensitic transformation; (220) peak FWHM = 0.776°; microstrain = 5.1 × 10^-3; dislocation density = 7.9 × 10^14 m^-2 for CR 50%
characterization_methods.purpose: identify phases and quantify peak broadening, microstrain and dislocation density

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JSM7200F SEM equipped with EBSD system
characterization_methods.key_findings: EBSD analysis reported for undeformed, CR 30% and CR 90% conditions; no CR 50%-specific LAGB fraction or texture value is individually reported in the text
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrochemical polishing in electrolyte containing perchloric acid (5%) and acetic acid (95%) at 50 V for 30 s
characterization_methods.purpose: characterize grain orientations, boundary misorientation and local misorientation (KAM)

analytical_models.equation_role: relate XRD diffraction peak broadening to grain size and microstrain
analytical_models.model_note: β_τ = Kλ/(D cosθ) + 4ε tanθ; through fitting analysis, microstrain for CR 50% = 5.1 × 10^-3

analytical_models.equation_role: calculate dislocation density from average grain size and microstrain
analytical_models.model_note: ρ = 2√3 (ε^2)^(1/2) / (D b); CR 50% dislocation density = 7.9 × 10^14 m^-2

computational_details.simulation_method: XRD line profile analysis (Williamson–Hall) and dislocation density calculation
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: dislocation density trend aligns with TEM observations (Figure 3)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: dislocation entanglement and walls emerge due to interactions between dislocations at 50% CR reduction; a significant amount of deformation twins is observed

interfaces.phase_evolution: single-phase austenite maintained throughout CR; no deformation-induced martensitic phase transformation
interfaces.slip_behavior: distinct characteristics of dislocation plane slip vanish at 50% CR reduction; deformation twinning is activated

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Prior to CR, all specimens underwent solution treatment at 1000°C for 1 h and were then water-quenched to room temperature.

Test steels immersed in liquid nitrogen for 3–5 min; after cooling, individual specimen rapidly removed for single pass rolling with thickness reduction about 2%; then promptly re-immersed in liquid nitrogen; steps repeated until cumulative thickness reduction reached 50%.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped tensile specimens with standard distance segment of 20 × 5 × 1 mm, machined along RD

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: engineering stress–strain curve for CR 50% condition shown in Figure 8a

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: loading 500 g; dwelling time 15 s; HV values averaged from at least 5 measurements

defects.type: dislocation entanglement, dislocation walls, deformation twins

phases_present.morphology: flattened/banded elongated grains along RD with dense slip bands

structures.overall_structure: flattened/banded elongated grains with dense slip bands; dislocation entanglement and dislocation walls; significant amount of deformation twins; single-phase austenitic (no deformation-induced martensitic transformation)

unmapped_findings: SFE of this steel: 72 mJ m^-2 at room temperature and 51 mJ m^-2 at cryogenic temperature (b0044).

At moderate strains (50% CR reduction), twinning is described as the main plastic deformation mechanism, while dislocation plane slip diminishes and dislocation walls plus deformation twins become visible (b0023, b0044).
CR 50% is one of the four cumulative thickness reduction states studied (30%, 50%, 70%, 90%) (b0012).
The CR 50% sample exhibits a strength-ductility trade-off relative to the undeformed state: UTS 1518 MPa, YS 1379 MPa, elongation 8.8%, microhardness 479 HV (figure_008).
